claims.text: A direct W/CuCrZr interface suffers from mismatched thermal expansion under high heat flux and radiation.
A direct W/CuCrZr interface suffers from diffusion-related issues under high heat flux and radiation.
A thin Mo layer can be deposited between W and CuCrZr by a technique such as physical vapor deposition.
Mo has a thermal expansion coefficient intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
A Mo interlayer mediates interfacial stress between W and CuCrZr.
A Mo interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier between W and CuCrZr.
Mo reduces mechanical strain by accommodating differential thermal expansion between W and CuCrZr.
Mo is chemically compatible with the W/CuCrZr joint.
The chemical compatibility of Mo inhibits detrimental interfacial reactions in a W/CuCrZr joint.
A Mo interlayer inhibits interdiffusion between W and CuCrZr.
A Mo interlayer improves adhesion relative to a direct W/CuCrZr interface.
A Mo interlayer reduces interfacial cracking relative to a direct W/CuCrZr interface.
A Mo interlayer enhances the durability of a W/CuCrZr joint under extreme fusion-reactor conditions.
Without an interlayer, W/CuCrZr bonding is prone to interfacial degradation caused by thermal stress.
Without an interlayer, diffusion-related degradation at a W/CuCrZr interface may cause premature failure under reactor conditions.
The beneficial effects of a Mo interlayer are expected within the operating-temperature and radiation-fluence limits of current fusion-reactor designs.
